mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces corporate profit growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods (UNRATE > 4.5%), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts and retail sales indicate strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through joint demand expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%), a decline in industrial production signals deteriorating supply conditions that increase input costs and reduce corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 5.0% and INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC for the regime-conditional signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 grows, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index exceeds 325.0, it signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods (CPIAUCSL > 325.0), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals worsening labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS declines, or the Rank IC for the regime-conditional signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and consumer price index indicate aggressive monetary tightening amid high inflation, which compresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.
